transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28 14:20 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Maya, Rafael, Priya (Redwood); Samir, Lena, Marcus, Tariq (Horizon MedTech)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we'll go through high level constraints then Priya will walk us through the network and deployment options. Rafael will cover the onboarding cadence.
[00:18] Samir (Horizon): Hi all, Samir here. We're excited, we want to get the inference path stable for our imaging pipeline, so low latency, secure, and auditable.
[00:28] Lena (Horizon): Lena - Platform. I'm the person who will actually configure the VPC peering and connect the load balancers. 
[00:35] Marcus (Horizon): Marcus - security. My main focus is KMS, audit logs, and making sure we meet our SOC2 needs.
[00:42] Priya (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda: (1) network prerequisites (VPC, peering, routes, egress), (2) deployment options (hosted vs private dedicated vs on-prem), (3) key management and logging, (4) pilot scope and timeline.

[02:05] Priya: On the networking side, we typically support VPC peering or private link in the cloud provider. For on-prem we do an appliance approach. Which are you leaning toward?
[02:18] Tariq (Horizon): We're leaning private deployment inside our AWS account — so VPC peering. We can't expose data to public internet, egress is a concern.
[02:27] Priya: Ok that's common. We'll need the subnet CIDRs, routing table access, and we'll ask you to open specific ports for the peering endpoint. I'll send a checklist but at a high level it's TCP 443 and the internal peering CIDR routes. Sometimes the KV cache calls create more ephemeral connections — we call out those ranges in the doc.
[02:56] Samir: When you say KV cache what do you mean? Will that leak anything? There's been confusion in our security reviews.
[03:07] Priya: Sorry, bad shorthand — K-V cache, as in the model's key-value cache for sequence decoding; it's internal to the runtime and not persisted to disk by default, but we can configure retention. It doesn't send training data anywhere.
[03:25] Marcus: We will want full control over keys — BYOK. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or an HSM?
[03:32] Priya: Yes, we have BYOK patterns. We integrate with customer KMS for private deployments, and for Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key via our control plane integration. For hosted tenants there's a managed option but for you we can do KMS-backed key access with IAM roles. Note: HSM integration is an extra step, we typically coordinate with platform ops for cert exchange.
[03:58] Marcus: And audit logs? Retention? We might need 13 months.
[04:05] Rafael (Redwood): We export audit logs to a customer-owned S3 or secure syslog; retention is configurable. For Private deployments we can set retention to whatever your policy needs, and we can produce SOC2 artifacts. We'll link the compliance pack after this call.

[05:10] Priya: On performance: Samir mentioned imaging pipeline. What's your latency SLO per inference and expected qps?
[05:21] Samir: Ideally under 200ms 95th pctl for the core model at 1-2 requests per second per device, aggregated maybe 5k concurrent inference sessions during peaks — but initial pilot is smaller, 200-500 rps.
[05:38] Priya: Ok. For that we'd probably recommend dedicated capacity with batching turned off for strict latency, or a small dedicated pool with extremely short batch windows. We'll run estimates for CPU/GPU sizing. There's tradeoffs on cost: lower batching increases cost.
[05:58] Samir: Cost is a big factor; we have internal model infra too and we want to compare unit economics.
[06:05] Maya: Totally — we'll put together a cost/throughput spreadsheet with a few configurations (hosted burst, dedicated pool, private on-prem) and show per-token or per-inference costs and latency profiles.

[07:10] Lena: Network-wise: do you require VPC peering or can we do AWS PrivateLink? Sometimes our security team prefers PrivateLink to avoid routing changes.
[07:19] Priya: Both are possible. PrivateLink reduces lateral routing exposure but has different endpoints and NAT considerations; peering is simpler for larger internal traffic. We'll document the differences in the checklist.

[08:00] Marcus: A few compliance questions: 1) Data residency — can you guarantee EU region only for model serving? 2) Role-based access controls — how granular?
[08:11] Rafael: For Redwood Private you can pin region to EU-only; we can enforce tenancy and model location. For RBAC we support teams, roles, and token-scoped permissions, and you can sync via SAML SSO for identity.
[08:28] Marcus: SAML or SSO is fine; we use Okta. We'll want SCIM provisioning ideally.
[08:34] Priya: Okta + SAML + SCIM is supported for enterprise tenants; we'll capture the SSO config steps in the runbook.

[09:20] Samir: About model versions — we may want to roll forward a new quantized variant if latency improves. How do rollouts work?
[09:29] Priya: We have rollout policies: canary % rollouts, automatic fallback to a lower-capacity variant, and model pinning for a route. For private deployments you control version pins via the control plane and we can automate A/B traffic splits.
[09:44] Samir: Great. For the pilot, we want a safety rollback if quality regresses.
[09:49] Priya: We'll include health checks and evaluation hooks. Also optional: Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles but for now we'll stick to verified variants.

[11:05] Tariq: On connectivity tests — do you provide a staging endpoint we can smoke-test from our VPC before cutover?
[11:13] Priya: Yes, we provision a staging endpoint in your account or in a partner account and perform an OTAP test. We'll also run a certificate exchange test for keys.

[12:30] Maya: Timeline proposal: onboarding kickoff now; network & compliance docs by end of week; technical deep-dive with Priya next week; pilot kickoff in two weeks pending network setup. Thoughts?
[12:45] Lena: That fits our calendar. We need at least 5 business days to get firewall exceptions approved.
[12:52] Marcus: Security will need to review the SOC2 pack and the key exchange flow, please send by Friday.

[14:00] Rafael: I'll own the pilot runbook and stakeholder invites. Priya will lead the deep technical. Maya will coordinate pricing and contract touches.

[15:10] Samir: Quick question — about logs, can we get token-level cost attribution back to our app user id? We want billing breakdown aligned to request IDs.
[15:23] Priya: We can emit per-request trace IDs and cost metadata; you'll need to supply request correlation IDs on the client so it ties together. We'll include an example in the runbook.

[16:40] Maya: Ok let's recap real quick: Rafael to send runbook and SOC2 pack; Priya to send network checklist and cost estimate; Priya to schedule SE deep-dive; Horizon to share CIDRs and timeline. We'll reconvene after the deep-dive.
[17:02] Marcus: Sounds good. Anything else?
[17:08] Maya: No, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with calendar invites.

[17:20] (crosstalk)

End meeting.
